newsitem.title: USA: Wells Fargo expects to meet savings target.
newsitem.headline: Wells Fargo expects to meet savings target.

text.p: Wells Fargo and Co Chairman Paul Hazen said Tuesday he was confident the company would achieve expected savings in 1997 from its merger with First Interstate Bancorp.
He was referring to targeted expense savings of $800 million annually.

"Our expenses this (1996 fourth) quarter were high and reflect the costs of completing the conversion of First Interstate's customer base to a common set of systems and products," Hazen said in a release accompanying Wells Fargo's fourth quarter results.
Wells Fargo reported fourth quarter net income of $1.12 per share, versus $6.29 a year earlier.
Since its 1996 fourth quarter results reflect the effects of the First Interstate merger, they are not comparable to year-ago results, the company said.
Non-interest expense in the fourth quarter was $1.488 billion and included an estimated $300 million in integration-related expenses.
A year earlier, non-interest expense totalled $563 million, a spokeswoman said.
Wells Fargo's loan loss provision was $70 million in the 1996 fourth quarter, and $105 million for the full year.
Net charge-offs totalled $178 million in the fourth quarter, including $101 million in the credit card category.
Wells Fargo shares were up 2-1/8 to 281-7/8.
